overview: Iran is a country in Western Asia, between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf. Its capital and largest city is Tehran. Iran, long known as Persia, is home to one of the world's oldest civilisations, and the ancient Persian Empire was among the largest in history. Since the 1979 revolution it has been an Islamic republic. Persian, also called Farsi, is the official language.

geography.text: Most of Iran is a high central plateau ringed by mountains: the Alborz in the north, where Damavand is the highest peak, and the long Zagros range in the west. The centre has two great deserts, the Dasht-e Kavir and the Dasht-e Lut, one of the hottest places on Earth. The north coast on the Caspian Sea is green and wet, while the south faces the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

history.text: Iran is home to one of the world's oldest civilisations. Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire in the 500s BC, one of the largest the world had seen. Islam arrived in the 600s, and under the Safavids in the 1500s Shia Islam became the state religion. In 1979 a revolution overthrew the Shah and created the Islamic Republic.

events.title: Persian Empire
events.text: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire.

events.title: Arab conquest
events.text: The last Persian empire falls and Islam spreads.

events.title: Safavid dynasty
events.text: The Safavids make Shia Islam the state religion.

events.title: Iran–Iraq War
events.text: Iraq invades Iran, starting an eight-year war.

government.text: Iran is an Islamic republic. The Supreme Leader, a senior cleric, holds the highest power and controls the armed forces and courts. Ali Khamenei has held the role since 1989. Voters elect a President and parliament, but a council of clerics and lawyers decides who may stand. Mass protests in 2022, led by women, were harshly suppressed.

economy.text: Iran has some of the world's largest reserves of oil and natural gas. International sanctions over its nuclear programme have limited its oil exports and access to world banks, causing high inflation. It also exports petrochemicals, steel, pistachios and saffron.

culture.text: Iran, also known as Persia, has a history of more than 2,500 years as a state. Persian poets such as Hafez, Rumi and Ferdowsi are loved by Iranians today. Persian carpets, miniature paintings and Nowruz, the Persian New Year at the spring equinox, are world-famous.

items.title: Persepolis
items.text: The ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, built from 518 BC.

items.title: Nowruz
items.text: New Year at the spring equinox, celebrated across Central Asia.

items.title: Persian carpets
items.text: Hand-knotted rugs, a craft thousands of years old.

sport.text: Football is Iran's most popular sport, and Iran has played at several World Cups. Wrestling is the traditional sport, with many Olympic golds, and Iran is strong in weightlifting and volleyball.

items.text: Iran beat the United States at the World Cup.

items.title: Zurkhaneh
items.text: Traditional 'house of strength' training, listed by UNESCO.

didYouKnow: Iran has one of the world's oldest continuous civilisations.
The game of polo may have begun in ancient Persia.
